rank.note: the live-books-cheapest-travel shape, offline: the eleven Travel-category prices enumerated by extract_all, reduced to the cheapest in code. Prices are that case's own hand-verified ground truth (minimum £23.21, 'The Road to Little Dribbling'). This is the reduction that has to exist for that case to be answerable at all — the deployed run 734d3d1f planned 'read article 0' and returned the FIRST price instead. PR #29 R2 briefly gated the agent's call on `is_aggregate`, which this wording misses, so the raw list was published instead; R9 moved the gate into `rank` and this shape is reachable again (extract-all-cheapest-wording-still-reduces is its end-to-end twin).
rank.task: In the Travel category, find the cheapest book and tell me its exact price.

rank.note: same list, opposite direction — 'most expensive' must not be read as the 'most' branch's mode over strings.
rank.task: Which book in this category is the most expensive?

rank.note: probe #3's shape: non-numeric values, so 'most' counts rather than compares.

rank.note: the counting direction inverts too — and the least-quoted author here is unique, so it is a rank and not a tie.
rank.task: Which author has the fewest quotes listed on this page?

rank.note: a tie is ambiguous and must be loud, the same ruling near-equidistant-is-ambiguous made for the resolver. Returning either name would be a confident wrong answer, which is the defect family this milestone exists to close.

rank.note: no superlative in the task: the enumeration IS the answer and must survive untouched (multi-row list answers, contract: answer string|list).

rank.note: a single-element enumeration reduces to its one element — nothing to compare, and no tie.
rank.task: Which author has the most quotes listed on this page?

rank.note: cold review, M31: a price column with one non-numeric cell used to fall through to the counting branch, so the REPEATED price won 'highest' as a confident success. Mixed columns refuse, the same way a tie does.

rank.note: the worse direction of the same defect: 'cheapest' over the mode branch picks the unique junk cell, and the tie guard never fires because it really is a unique winner. 'Out of stock' as a price, reported as success.

rank.note: PR #29 R9's other side: the task asks for the enumeration itself, so the ranking word in it is describing an ORDER, not selecting one row. Same values, same `_RANK` word, opposite answer — which is why the rule is a property of the task's request, not of the answer's shape.
rank.task: List every product in the catalogue with its price, cheapest first.

rank.note: `\blist\b` must not match 'listed' — probe #3's own question contains it and is a single-answer ranking. This row is the boundary that keeps probe3-quotes-most-quoted-author green.
rank.task: Which author has the most quotes listed on this page?

rank.note: 'all' is deliberately NOT an enumerate-request word: 'of all the products' is a comparison frame, not a request for all of them, and treating it as one would publish the raw list for a single-answer question — the exact R9 defect.
rank.task: Of all the products here, which one is the cheapest?

expect.note: each row is (task, enumerated values, the reduction code must produce; null means the reduction must refuse)

provenance: M31. `extract_all` returns a list; the question asked for one item. The reduction is the half of the M31 spec that says rank/compare/count stays in code and never in the LLM, and it is what makes probe3-quotes-most-quoted-author and live-books-cheapest-travel answerable. Unit-shaped rather than end-to-end because the interesting failures are in the reduction rules (numbers vs counts, direction, ties, no-op), and a browser run per row would buy nothing and cost wall clock the fast suite does not have.

triage.note: tagged invariant: the ranking is the only place in this system where code, not the model, decides which of several real values is THE answer. Watched red first, before `verifier.rank` existed: `ImportError: cannot import name 'rank' from 'src.browser.verifier'` — the same shape the `aggregate` probe key was watched red as, since _run_verifier_case had no `rank` key either until its milestone. Rows 8 and 9 came from the M31 cold review and were watched red against the implementation as first written (`if all(nums)` falling through to the counting branch): row 8 returned '$19.99' and row 9 returned 'Out of stock', both as answers rather than refusals. PR #29 R9 added rows 10-12 for the enumerate-request rule that decides whether `rank` reduces at all. Row 10 is the one that goes red at THIS level — with the `_ENUMERATE_REQUEST` gate removed it returns 'Cobalt Floor Rug $18.00' where the task asked for every product. Rows 11 and 12 are boundary rows that pass either way; they exist so a later widening of that regex (adding 'listed', or 'all') turns red here instead of in production. The R2-gate defect rows 1 and 12 describe was never visible at this level at all — that gate lived at the agent's call site, so its red is end-to-end and belongs to extract-all-cheapest-wording-still-reduces.
